für unsere Verwaltung in Leipzig
Kennziffer: M-01
Die Doceins Gruppe ist ein Zusammenschluss von Medizinischen Versorgungszentren (MVZ) an über 50 Standorten deutschlandweit. Insgesamt 470 Ärzte und medizinische Fachkräfte arbeiten tagtäglich daran, als das medizinische Netzwerk der Region eine flächendeckende und optimale Patientenversorgung zu ermöglichen.
Gemeinsam können wir viel individueller auf die Bedürfnisse jeder einzelnen zu behandelnden und zugewiesenen Person eingehen - mit wenig Bürokratie und einem interdisziplinären Team, das in der Region verankert ist und die Patienten und Patientinnen noch persönlich kennt.
An unserem zentralen Verwaltungsstandort in Leipzig arbeiten wir mit Leidenschaft daran, die Rahmenbedingungen für eine optimale Patientenversorgung zu schaffen.
Dabei setzen wir auf Teamgeist, kurze Entscheidungswege und echte Wertschätzung - sowohl gegenüber unseren Patientinnen und Patienten als auch gegenüber unseren Mitarbeitenden. Zur Verstärkung unseres HR-Teams suchen wir zum nächstmöglichen Zeitpunkt einen/eine Personalreferent/in (m/w/d) in Vollzeit (35-40 Stunden/Woche). Bringen Sie Ihr Know-how und Ihre Persönlichkeit ein und gestalten Sie mit uns gemeinsam eine moderne und menschliche Personalarbeit.
Wir versorgen Patienten. Gem eins am.

Deine Aufgaben
Standort: München, hybrid (2 Tage/Woche im Office, Rest remote) · Befristet bis Ende Februar 2028 · 30–40 Stunden/Woche
Für unser People & Organization Team in München suchen wir einen Senior People Operations Specialist (m/w/d) zur Vertretung während einer Elternzeit, befristet bis Ende Februar 2028. Diese individual Contributor (IC) Rolle berichtet direkt an den VP People & Organization und hat ihren Schwerpunkt auf Deutschland.
Du übernimmst gemeinsam mit unserer bestehenden People Operations Managerin die operative Verantwortung für People Operations und stellst operative Exzellenz im Employee Lifecycle sicher. Du agierst eigenständig auf Senior-Niveau, bringst tiefe fachliche Expertise mit und übernimmst Verantwortung für komplexe Workstreams unserer P&O-Agenda.
Du fungierst als erfahrene Stimme im Team und bringst eigene Standards für Qualität, Compliance und Employee Experience ein.
Du verantwortest komplexe und sensible Themen im Employee Lifecycle eigenständig, von schwierigen Vertragssituationen über Sonderkonstellationen bis zu mehrdeutigen Befristungs-, Teilzeit- oder Elternzeitfällen.
Du bist fachlicher Ansprechpartner für vertragliche und sozialversicherungsrechtliche Fragestellungen und arbeitest souverän mit externen Beratern (z.B. Steuerberater, Anwaltskanzlei).
Du treibst den Aufbau unserer Compliance-Themen (Datenschutz, Mutterschutz, etc.) eigenverantwortlich voran und steuerst die Umsetzung mit hoher Eigenständigkeit.
Du leitest komplexe P&O-OKR-Workstreams und Projekte mit Gestaltungsspielraum von Konzeption bis Rollout und gestaltest die Weiterentwicklung unserer Prozesse durch Technologie und KI aktiv mit.
Du übernimmst Sparring und Mentoring für weniger erfahrene Kollegen im Team.
Was Du mitbringst
Abgeschlossenes Studium im Bereich BWL, Psychologie, Personalmanagement, Arbeitsrecht oder einer vergleichbaren Fachrichtung.
Mindestens 6 Jahre Berufserfahrung in der operativen Personalarbeit, idealerweise in einem dynamischen, internationalen Umfeld mit hybrider oder remote Arbeitsweise, inkl. eigenverantwortlicher Steuerung von HR-Projekten (z.B. Compliance-Aufbau, Systemmigration oder Prozessoptimierung).
Fundierte Kenntnisse im deutschen Arbeits- und Sozialversicherungsrecht. Du kannst komplexe Fälle eigenständig einschätzen, inkl. Kündigungsschutz, AGG-Vorgängen und sozialversicherungsrechtlichen Fragen.
Erweiterte Kenntnisse im Umgang mit KI-Tools im HR-Kontext.
Hohe inhaltliche Eigenständigkeit, ausgeprägtes Urteilsvermögen und Sicherheit im Umgang mit sensiblen Themen und Stakeholdern auf Leitungsebene. Diskretion, professionelle Distanz, klare Kommunikation und Freude an Aufbauarbeit.
Verhandlungssichere Deutschkenntnisse und gute bis sehr gute Englischkenntnisse.
Was wir Dir bieten
Verantwortungsvolle, spannende und abwechslungsreiche Aufgaben mit viel Gestaltungsspielraum in einem dynamischen Unternehmen , das flache Hierarchien und eine offene, lockere Arbeitsatmosphäre lebt, in der alle per "Du" sind
Ein freundliches, offenes Team bestehend aus ca. 450 Mitarbeitenden in Deutschland, UK und Belgien mit mehreren lieben Bürohunden an unseren Standorten
Flexible Arbeitszeiten (die auf Vertrauensarbeitszeit basieren), Home-Office Optionen inkl. Kostenbeteiligung an Deiner Home-Office Ausstattung und die Möglichkeit, für mehrere Monate aus dem Ausland zu arbeiten
28 Tage Urlaubsanspruch sowie die Möglichkeit, bis zu 20 Tage unbezahlten Urlaub sowie Sonderurlaub zu nehmen!
Zugang zu modernen KI-Tools: Wir stellen Dir moderne KI-Tools zur Verfügung, die Dich dabei unterstützen, effizienter zu arbeiten, neue Ideen zu entwickeln und Deine Fähigkeiten in einer sich stetig wandelnden digitalen Welt weiter auszubauen.
Verschiedene interne & externe Weiterentwicklungsmöglichkeiten , die Du eigenständig nach Deinen Interessen auswählen kannst
Deine mentale Gesundheit ist uns wichtig! Deshalb kannst Du im Rahmen der Plattform " OpenUp " anonym an Einzel- oder Gruppentherapie-Sitzungen teilnehmen oder in 1:1 Meetings mit echten Therapeuten sprechen
EGYM Wellpass Mitgliedschaft: Mit unserer bezuschussten Mitgliedschaft beim EGYM Wellpass erhältst Du Zugang zu tausenden Sport- und Wellnesseinrichtungen – darunter Fitnessstudios, Schwimmbäder, Kletterhallen, Yoga- und Pilatesstudios sowie viele weitere Angebote. So kannst Du flexibel und deutschlandweit etwas für Deine Fitness und Dein Wohlbefinden tun – ganz so, wie es am besten in Deinen Alltag passt!
Verschiedene Mitarbeiterrabatte - für Mensch und Tier!
Regelmäßige Team-, Company- und Family & Friends- Events
Du brauchst eine Pause? Entspanne Dich in unserer Social-Area, die mit einem Kicker ausgestattet ist oder fordere Deine Kollegen auf unserer gemütlichen Sofalandschaft zu einem Mario Kart-Battle (oder einem anderen Nintendo Switch Spiel) heraus!
Aufgewärmtes Essen magst Du nicht? Essen bestellen dauert Dir zu lange? In unserem Büro steht Dir eine hochwertige, vollausgestattete Küche zur Verfügung in der Du den Kochlöffel schwingen oder tolle Kuchen zaubern kannst!
Kaffee, Kakao, Tee und weitere kühle Softdrinks wie Wasser und Säfte sowie frisches Obst, kleinere Snacks und eine prall gefüllte Süßigkeiten-Schublade stehen Dir kostenlos zur Verfügung
Viele weitere, großartige Benefits die wir Dir gerne im Rahmen des Recruitingprozesses näher vorstellen!

The United States Space Force (USSF) Civilian Talent Management Office (CTMO) at Joint Base San Antonio, Texas is searching for Human Resources Information Systems Specialist (NH-0201-03, GS 12/13 equivalent). Description: As a Human Resources Specialist for the U.S.

Space Force, you will serve as a technical expert and data innovator at the heart of the Civilian Talent Management Office, shaping how the service builds its elite workforce.

In this dynamic role, you will lead challenging projects to design, analyze, and automate critical human capital processes by harnessing the power of advanced data systems like PowerBI, Business Objects (BOXi), Defense Civilian Personnel Data System (DCPDS), Manpower Programming and Execution System (MPES), myFSS, USA Staffing, and PowerApps.

By transforming raw HR data into actionable intelligence, you will create sophisticated reports, deliver high-impact briefings to senior Space Force leaders, and develop innovative solutions to complex organizational challenges, ensuring that the USSF can recruit, hire, and retain the nation's top talent.

If you are a proactive problem-solver with a passion for data and a drive to build the workforce of the future, apply today to make your mark on the newest branch of the armed forces.

The ideal candidate is a seasoned and proactive Human Resources data expert with a proven mastery of federal HR information systems, particularly PowerBI, Business Objects (BOXi), Defense Civilian Personnel Data System (DCPDS), Manpower Programming and Execution System (MPES), myFSS, USA Staffing, and PowerApps.

This individual possesses an innate ability to not only extract and manipulate complex datasets but also to conduct deep-dive analyses, turning raw data into actionable intelligence and strategic recommendations for senior leadership.

As a natural problem-solver and leader, they are adept at independently managing projects, developing automated solutions for HR processes, and mentoring junior team members.

Their exceptional communication skills allow them to translate highly technical information into clear, compelling briefings and to build strong collaborative relationships across various DAF, Field Command, and installation organizations.

Ultimately, this professional is a forward-thinking innovator who combines deep knowledge of federal HR principles with advanced technical skill to drive data-centric decision-making and enhance the operational effectiveness of the U.S. Space Force. Key Skills and Abilities: 1.

Knowledge of a wide range of federal Human Resources (HR) laws, executive orders, regulations, policies, directives, instructions, and concepts governing HR functions. 2.

Knowledge of advanced federal human resources management (HRM) principles, concepts, practices, fact finding and analytical methods, a wide range of qualitative and quantitative techniques, and relationships of various HR disciplines as well as seasoned consultative skill sufficient to resolve complex HRM problems not susceptible to treatment by standard methods. 3.

Knowledge of databases, higher-order programming tools and retrieval languages associated with the HR information system(s) and system capabilities, procedures, limitations and retrieval options. 4. Knowledge of organizational structures, missions, objectives, operating programs, key positions, and administrative/protocol policies and procedures. 5.

Skill in conducting reviews and analyzing and assessing HR data analytics to include identifying deficiencies; measuring compliance, consistency, and effectiveness; and making recommendations for enhancements and improvements. 6.

Ability to communicate both orally and in writing and to establish and maintain effective and positive working relationships.

This position is located in the Military Personnel Office (MILPO) of the Army National Guard (ARNG).

The purpose of this position is to supervise and manage two or more of the following human resource programs: Health Services Program, to include Line of Duty (LOD), Incapacitation Pay (INCAP), Warrior Transition Unit (WTU), Active Duty Medical Extension (ADME), Medical Retention Processing 2 (MRP2), and Medical Boards to include MOS Medical Review Board (MMRB), Medical Evaluation Board (MEB), and Physical Evaluation Board (PEB).

Directly supervises and provides technical and administrative supervision over Human Resources Assistants (Military), Human Resources Specialists (Military), and specialist within the other specialized functions of the MILPO office.

Formulates human resources and administrative procedures and policies based on the interpretation of regulations and directives from Department of Defense (DoD), Department of Army (DA), and the National Guard Bureau (NGB).

As required, performs military human resources work in any of the program areas, for which assigned, for officer, warrant officer, and enlisted members and includes but is not limited to: processing and reporting on status of LOD investigations, formal and informal; processing INCAP pay; processing and providing quality control of MRP2 and ADME packets; providing oversight and tracking of personnel assigned to WTU; providing oversight to Tricare and Military Medical Support Office (MMSO) and coordinating for treatment and follow-on authorization of care; coordinating fit for duty evaluations; processing Soldiers for entrance into the MEB and PEB; tracking medically non-deployable Soldier status within the State; working in coordination with the Medical Detachment in the training of Medical Readiness NCOs; providing oversight of the medical travel and orders program; working in conjunction with the PDHRA program; directing, organizing, and planning staff assistance visits and Command Inspection Program activities.

Convenes or participates in various boards which may include: MOS Medical Review Board (MMRB), Incapacitation Review Boards, Medical and/or Physical evaluations, etc. Plans, organizes, and directs the activities of assigned program areas, ensuring that legal and regulatory requirements are met.

Develops goals and objectives that integrate organization and military human resources objectives and establishes policies and procedures for accomplishment of the same. Coordinates, plans, and schedules with other organization managers and customers as appropriate.

Reviews and provides advice on organization missions, functions, and manning of serviced units. Identifies, analyzes, and provides recommendations to supervisor on significant issues and problems related to work accomplishment.

Identifies requirements and initiates requests for additional resources including personnel, overtime, equipment, supplies, and space to ensure success in meeting goals and objectives. Establishes analysis systems to ensure actions are timely and reviewed at critical points. Accepts, amends, or rejects work presented by subordinates.

Plans and schedules work in a manner that promotes a smooth flow and even distribution, sets and adjusts short-term priorities, and prepares schedules.

Assigns work to subordinate employees based on organization priorities and consideration of difficulty and requirements of assignments such that the experience, training, and abilities of staff are effectively utilized to meet organization and customer needs.

Provides advice, guidance, and direction to employees on a wide range of military human resources and administrative issues.

Interviews candidates for positions and selects, or recommends selection of, candidates for vacancies, promotions, details, and reassignments in consideration of skills and qualifications, mission requirements, and EEO objectives. Hears and resolves employee complaints and refers serious unresolved complaints to higher-level management.

As a Human Resources Officer, you will: Exercise full administrative authority for employees assigned to the Office, including subordinate supervisors, in accomplishing objectives and fulfilling program demands.

Participate in operational planning with top level management to determine the effect of proposed changes to the human resources management programs.

Direct a program and staff concerned with providing advice and guidance, and administering the following human resources functions: development of personnel policies applicable Bureau-wide; labor relations and negotiations for Bureau-wide coverage and local issues; employee relations to include performance and awards management; discipline; employee training and development; staffing services to include, recruitment and outreach, OPM certification requests, merit promotion, special hiring authorities; pay-setting and administration; position management and classification services; benefits and services (health insurance, life insurance, retirement, incentive awards, external awards, etc.); HRIS ; SES program management; and special projects, serving as OHR coordinator for all functional areas on special, complex assignments and projects.

Serve as advisor to Senior executives, managers and supervisors, and provides guidance and assistance to supervisors and employees on all areas of human resources management regulations, policies and laws.

Analyze and evaluate workforce plans, employment trends, budget development and implementation, complex-wide studies and human capital management assessment tools and programs.
You must meet the following requirements by the closing date of this announcement. For the GS-15, you must have one year of specialized experience at a level of difficulty and responsibility equivalent to the GS-14 grade level in the Federal service.

Specialized experience for this position includes: Advising leadership on workforce composition and long-range workforce planning strategies; AND Leading restructuring initiatives, consolidations, and realignment efforts to support evolving business needs; AND Supervising a staff of Human Resource professionals responsible for Staffing, Recruitment, and Classification functions; AND Leading labor union/management relations and bargaining negotiations; AND Guiding Human Resource policy development and compliance operations.

In addition to the above requirements, you must meet the following time-in-grade requirement, if applicable: For the GS-15, you must have been at the GS-14 level for 52 weeks.

You will serve as a staff advisor and consultant on the Labor Management Employee Relations (LMER) program.

Interpret and apply Federal pay and leave laws, regulations, and policies to advise managers, employees, and HR staff on compensation matters. Review, research, and resolve pay, leave, payroll, time and attendance, and personnel action issues while coordinating with payroll providers to ensure accurate and timely processing.

Advise on pay-setting actions and compensation flexibilities, including recruitment, relocation, and retention incentives, superior qualifications appointments, leave credit, and related authorities.

Analyze payroll and compensation data, identify trends, recommend process improvements, and prepare reports to support program performance and regulatory compliance. Collaborate with customer agencies, HR specialists, payroll providers, and employee representatives to resolve compensation issues and provide responsive customer service.

Develop or deliver guidance and training on compensation policies, payroll procedures, and pay and leave administration to managers, supervisors, and employees.
Minimum Qualifications for the GS-11 Grade Level: You qualify for the GS-11 grade level if you possess one full year of specialized experience comparable in scope and responsibility to the GS-09 grade level or pay band in the Federal service, obtained in either the public or private sectors, performing ALL the following duties: Assist and process routine payroll and compensation actions utilize pay/time and attendance automate systems; AND researching payroll and timekeeping records to support issue resolution; AND participating in compensation reviews; AND providing customer service and reporting support using established procedures and automated system (such as but not limited to GovTA, SLDCADA, Paycheck 8, HR Links, NFC, DFAS).

OR Have completed the requirements for a Ph.D. or equivalent doctoral degree or completed at least 3 full academic years of progressively higher-level graduate education leading to a Ph.D. or LL.M, if related, (for example, human resources, business, public administration, management or other directly related field of study) that demonstrates the knowledge, skills, and abilities required to do the work of this position.

OR Have a combination of education and experience to qualify at this level. To calculate your percentage of education, divide the number of graduate semester hours earned, in excess of 36 semester hours, by 18. If your education is in quarter hours, convert to semester hours by multiplying the number of quarter hours earned by 2/3rds.

To calculate your percentage of experience, divide the number of months of full-time experience by 12. If your experience was part-time, convert to full-time by dividing the number of hours worked per week by 40 then multiply by number of months worked. Add the percentages. The total must equal at least 100 percent to qualify.

(NOTE: You must submit a copy of your college transcripts (official or unofficial) to support your claim.) Minimum Qualifications for the GS-12 Grade Level: You qualify for the GS-12 grade level if you possess one full year of specialized experience comparable in scope and responsibility to the GS-11 grade level or pay band in the Federal service, obtained in either the public or private sectors, performing ALL the following duties: Assess pay, leave, timekeeping, work schedule, and compensation policies to resolve moderately complex employee pay and entitlement issues; AND analyze payroll, HR, and time and attendance records to identify pay discrepancies, determine root causes, take corrective actions, and coordinate resolutions with payroll service providers; AND administer compensation flexibilities, including recruitment, relocation, and retention incentives, differential pay, special pay, and pay-setting exceptions, relocation reimbursements, and service credit determinations; AND recommend process improvement to compensation and payroll through reviewing reports, identifying trends, audits, and conduct training Merit promotion applicants must meet the time-in-grade requirement as defined in 5 CFR 300, Subpart F.

One year at the 09 level is required to meet the time-in-grade requirements for the GS-11 level. Merit promotion applicants must meet the time-in-grade requirement as defined in 5 CFR 300, Subpart F. One year at the 11 level is required to meet the time-in-grade requirements for the GS-12 level.

What will I do in this position if hired? In this Human Resources Specialist position, you will be responsible for providing advice, assistance, and guidance to customers, supervisors, and managers.

The HR Specialist carries out these functions while exercising sound judgement, communicating effectively (both verbally and in writing), and exhibiting strong interpersonal and analytical skills.

Typical assignments include: Participate in the entire life cycle of FEMA's Local Hire Program including working with field leadership, hiring managers, and Headquarters through recruitment, interviews, and onboarding. Initiate, code and submit various personnel actions for local hires utilizing automated HR Information Systems (HRIS).

Utilize the Deployment Tracking System (DTS) to execute the deployment of personnel to and from disaster events and maintain their accountability while at a disaster event. Provide routine advice and assistance to managers and supervisors regarding the implementation and administration of the agency disaster performance evaluations.

Provide guidance to deployed Reservists on Federal Employee Health Benefits. What else do I need to know? At FEMA, our mission to help people before, during and after disasters; so, every employee at FEMA has a role in emergency management.

Every FEMA employee has regular and recurring emergency management responsibilities, though not every position requires routine deployment to disaster sites.

All positions are subject to recall around the clock for emergency management operations, which may require irregular work hours, work at locations other than the official duty station, and may include duties other than those specified in the employee's official position description.

Travel requirements in support of emergency operations may be extensive in nature (weeks to months), with little advance notice, and may require employees to relocate to emergency sites with physically austere and operationally challenging conditions. As a Reservist Employee, your role is to support response or recovery efforts.

Reservists are intermittent, on-call employees. Please note that this is not a full-time position, and you only are paid when deployed. Deployment frequency and length varies based on disaster response need.

Due to the irregular nature of disasters, Reservist employees are not guaranteed regular recurring hours, deployments, or renewal of employment.

The Civilian Reservist Emergency Workforce (CREW) Act protects the job rights of FEMA Reservists while they are deployed to disasters, emergencies, and critical trainings by including FEMA Reservists under the Uniformed Services Employment and Reemployments Rights Act (USERRA).

This means that if you hold another job, you are able to deploy as a FEMA reservist and your job will be protected. It also protects you against penalization, discrimination, or loss of employee benefits as a result of your deployments to disasters, emergencies, and critical trainings.

For more information, please visit FEMA.gov/careers or review the USERRA Resources from the Department of Labor.

Here at The Exploration Company, we are developing, producing, and operating Nyx, a modular and reusable space orbital vehicle that can eventually be refuelled in orbit and that can carry cargo - and potentially humans in the longer run.
"If you want to build a rocket, don't assign tasks — ignite a longing for the endless immensity of the stars."
This is not an ordinary workplace
We build space vehicles for humanity. Not as a tagline. Not as a marketing line. As the literal, daily reality of every person on our team. We are in the middle of a space exploration renaissance, one that happens once in a generation.

In just four years, we built two demonstrator capsules, signed a Space Act Agreement with NASA (the first European company ever to do so), booked 10 missions, and began developing Storm, a high-thrust staged combustion rocket engine. We operate across seven countries, backed by tier-one investors. And we are just getting started.

If you join TEC, you are not taking a job. You are choosing an expedition.
Our mission: We build space vehicles for humanity, enabling everyone to participate peacefully in the building of our human future in space.
Why you might not join us and why the right person will
1. We work on-site, together. Minimum three days a week in person, full presence. We'll always work with real life but our baseline is genuine commitment. If you need a fully remote role, we're probably not the right fit right now.
2. We are in build season. The pace is high, the stakes are real, the urgency is genuine. Steady and comfortable won't feel like enough here.
3. We expect extreme ownership. We want people who feel the mission personally, who care about Nyx, Storm and what we're building beyond their job description. This culture asks a lot. Willingly.
But if this excites you more than it worries you, few people get the chance to work on something history will remember. Nobody climbs Everest without full commitment. Nobody builds a space capsule or a rocket engine without it either. This is that moment. This is that team.

CodePath is the largest educator of college computer science students in the country. We've trained over 40,000 students from 1,000+ universities, and our partners include Amazon, Google, and other leading technology companies. We've spent nearly a decade training the next generation of technical talent, and we just launched a $150M initiative with Anthropic, building one of the most ambitious AI workforce programs in the world.
We're now expanding into new markets and scaling our team so we can move at the speed AI is transforming the workforce. People joining CodePath now will have the opportunity to help architect the next frontier of our work.
We believe technical skill is the fastest way to turn raw talent into real opportunity. We train the engineers the AI era runs on, building toward millions of learners, hundreds of millions in revenue, and billions in economic impact. If you want to own something and be part of a 0-to-1 journey at an organization moving at the speed of AI, this is the place to build it.

Location: Remote (U.S.)
Role Type: Full-Time
Reporting to: Head of People

Manages: A pod of early-talent recruiters plus fractional HR coordination support
Key Activities
Claude Corps is a fellowship that places early-career technologists inside nonprofits, government agencies, and public-interest organizations to build AI solutions that keep working after the fellow leaves. It runs as a partnership between Anthropic, CodePath, and Social Finance, backed by a $150M initiative with Anthropic. CodePath is the Employer of Record: we own the full fellow lifecycle, from recruiting and selection through employment, onboarding, benefits, and host support.
Cohort 1 places 100 fellows. The program scales toward 1,000 fellows in year one and 10,000 by year three. This role builds the pod that makes that scale real.
Why this role, now
Claude Corps needs one person accountable for how fellows get hired and how they get employed. Not a strategic HR seat at a distance from the work, and not a recruiting manager who hands off at the offer. A pod lead, running a small team that carries both.
You'll manage the recruiters screening early talent, and you'll manage the fractional HR coordination support that turns an accepted offer into a real employee. Where the program touches the person, you and the Claude Corps program managers work the case together: performance concerns, employee relations, a placement that isn't landing. You bring the process and the employment side. They bring the day-to-day context and the host relationship. Both names are on the outcome.
The math is the other half of the job. We go from 100 fellows to 1,000 to 10,000, and the pod does not grow 100x to match. A team this size clears that volume by building AI into the work: screening support, scheduling, candidate communication, onboarding packets, compliance tracking, the reporting that eats a coordinator's week. We train people to build with AI. We expect the people running our own operations to do the same.
The pod is small in Cohort 1. It grows with the cohorts, and how much it has to grow is partly up to you.
What you will own
Lead the pod . Manage the fractional early-talent recruiters and the HR coordinators supporting Claude Corps. Set the week's priorities, run the load-balancing when a cohort deadline compresses, coach against the bar, and grow the team's headcount and capability as cohorts scale. Fractional support means you are explicit about what you're buying with those hours and what falls to you.
Own screening and selection . Run the funnel from application review through offer, against the program's selection rubric and calibration process. Keep throughput honest: the pod moves volume, and you hold the line on signal quality and candidate experience while it does.
Own the employer-of-record lifecycle . Offers and e-sign, background checks, I-9 and work authorization, payroll setup, benefits enrollment, onboarding. Fellows are CodePath employees, and the experience should feel like it. You direct this work through the fractional coordinators rather than doing all of it yourself.
Use AI to hold the ratio . Find the repetitive work in recruiting and HR ops and get it automated or AI-assisted: resume screening support, interview scheduling, candidate comms, offer and onboarding document generation, multi-state compliance tracking, cohort reporting. Judgment calls stay with humans, and you decide where that line sits. Come with a bias toward trying things, and bring the team along so the whole pod works this way, not just you.
Co-own employee relations and performance with program management . When a fellow's performance or conduct needs attention, you and the program manager run it together. You own documentation, process, consistency, and the employment decisions that follow. The PM owns the host relationship and what's actually happening on the ground. Escalate to the Head of People when the situation warrants it, and know where that line is.
Build the systems . Turn one-cohort processes into repeatable operations: screening workflows, HR SLAs, multi-state compliance, and clean handoffs with our program partners. Bring a point of view on what to standardize and what to leave flexible while the program is still forming

5+ years across recruiting and HR or people operations, including time owning both, not just one
You've managed people, and you've managed through others' capacity, including contractors, shared services, or fractional support
You've run high-volume or early-talent hiring, and you've owned HR operations (payroll, benefits, compliance, onboarding). Employer-of-record, PEO, or multi-state employment experience is a strong plus
You already use AI in your own work and can point to something you automated or rebuilt with it. Comfort with ATS and HRIS configuration, workflow automation, and prompting is expected, not a bonus
You've handled employee relations and performance conversations, and you're steady in them
You're comfortable in a program that is still being built. You bring structure without waiting for someone else to hand it to you
You hold a high bar on quality and candidate experience at the same time
You communicate directly and work well across partner organizations with different systems and cultures
You care about the mission: expanding who gets to build with AI, and doing right by the people you employ
What success looks like
Each cohort is screened and hired on time, at target size, without cutting corners on signal quality
The employment lifecycle runs cleanly: offers, onboarding, payroll, and benefits land on time and compliant across every state we hire in
Cost and hours per fellow hired and onboarded drop cohort over cohort, because the work got automated and not because the team absorbed it
Performance and ER issues get handled early, documented consistently, and resolved with the program manager rather than around them
The pod grows in capability and ownership as the program scales, and the fractional support model either scales with it or you make the case for what replaces it

The following are the duties of this position at the full working level. If this vacancy includes more than one grade and you are selected at a lower grade level, you will have the opportunity to learn to perform these duties and receive training to help you grow in this position.

Responds to current and future needs within the orientation & experience program by implementing improvements to the program's automation, reports, and processes to deliver a successful program. Federal experience is not required. Experience may have been gained in the public sector, private sector or through Volunteer Service. One year of experience refers to full-time work; part-timework is considered on a prorated basis.

OR Superior Academic Achievement may be met by having a bachelor's degree, with one of the following: A GPA of 2.95 or higher on a 4.0 scale for all completed undergraduate courses or those completed in the last 2 years of study, or a GPA of 3.45 or higher on a 4.0 scale for all courses in the major field of study or those courses in the major completed in the last 2 years of study, or rank in the upper one third of the class in the college, university, or major subdivision, or membership in a national honor society recognized by the Association of College Honor Societies.

OR you may qualify with at least one (1) year of combined education and experience as defined above. OR you may qualify based on education as follows: A master's or equivalent graduate degree in a field of study that demonstrates the knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to do the work of this position such as: human resources, public administration, organizational psychology, or other administrative and management fields.

For this requirement, a competitive appointment is one where you applied to and were appointed from an announcement open to "All US Citizens" TIME IN GRADE (TIG): For positions above the GS-05, applicants must meet applicable time-in-­grade requirements to be considered eligible.

📍 Manchester, UK (Hybrid 4 days WFH) | 💰 £60,000 - £70,000
Street Group is a fast moving B2B SaaS business - grown in Manchester but on a UK wide mission to make moving house as easy as buying a car. We’ve recently raised Series B funding, and are scaling fast toward an ambitious growth plan - and we’re looking for a Senior People Partner to ensure we get there.
Over the past 6 years, our People team has designed, built, and implemented the people processes that have scaled Street Group from 30 - 230 people. But we know that systems that work at 150 people can break at 300 - and we want to get ahead of that.
This is an opportunity for someone who has been through that scaling journey before to have an oversized impact on a small but ambitious People team to become best in class.
If you know what can impact culture both positively and negatively as a company grows; have experience building systems that both set people up to do their best work AND that scale alongside the business; and embrace AI and the positive impact it can have on employee experience - we think you might do great work here.
Why this role exists now
Our People team is lean - and as we mature as a business, there’s limited capacity to ensure we’re constantly innovating and improving the mechanisms that enable people to do their best work. We have ambitious goals to achieve - now is the time to fine-tune our People function to ensure the business hits those goals.

In 2026, over half of the business told us they don't know what excellence looks like in their role, or how excellence is rewarded. This is the crux of this role; to build the systems, processes and reward that sets people up for success and ensure we reward and retain our best people.
Over the next 12-18 months, this will mean you'll be working with our Head of People and People Partner on initiatives that clarify excellence and reward - our internal levels framework, compensation & reward, embedding our excellence standard throughout the business, and coaching managers on a team by team basis to increase overall performance.

An experienced People Partner passionate about their craft; curious about how technology and innovation is changing the People landscape, and constantly looking for more impactful ways to support the business.
A commercial mindset - e.g. you measure your results on impact on business and team performance rather than work shipped.
An AI-native mindset: you treat AI as leverage and are keen to learn from our team, and share what’s been working for you - but understand the nuances of where AI can never replace genuine People Partnering.
The credibility and communication skills to bring busy managers on the journey with you.
Someone who makes the team better on purpose, not by accident: you share what you know and help develop the people around you.
Why you might not want to apply
We'd rather be honest up front, because this role won’t be for everyone.
If you want to move into people management. This is a senior IC role. You'll coach, share knowledge, and set standards, but you won't have direct reports. If a management title is what you're chasing now or in the imminent future, this isn’t the job for you.
If you haven't been through a similar scaling journey in SaaS businesses before. Our People team is home grown; we're specifically looking for the experience and knowledge that comes from having been there/done that before, and can prevent us from making common mistakes.
If AI feels like a threat rather than a tool. We love Claude Cowork, and have both built and used multiple other tools to improve and speed up our ways of working. We have a company-wide expectation that AI is utilised, so it will be a large part of this role.
If you want a role where you'll be spending a lot of time on pastoral employee interactions. This isn't going to be the main part of this role - you'll be spending most of your time building a culture of excellence.
If that list sounds like your kind of role, please apply and let us know why!
We recognise that women and people from underrepresented groups often apply for jobs only when they meet every single requirement listed. If you fall into that category and are about to rule yourself out based on the above criteria, please consider applying anyway. We'd love to see your application!

We’re an award-winning PropTech business based in Manchester, founded in 2015 by brother and sister duo, Tom & Heather Staff. Most of us have personal experience of how painful moving can be, and Tom and Heather saw an opportunity to change this: utilising technology, as well as our incredibly talented team, to improve the industry for everyone.
Our products, Street.co.uk , Spectre & Cortex form a powerful trio, working harmoniously together to transform an agent’s job. From securing more leads and winning new instructions to streamlining business operations and growing market share, our products are supercharging 1,000s of agencies across the UK.

About Logol
-----------
Logol is an international Swiss technology company operating in a dynamic and growing environment. As our business continues to develop we are looking for an **HR Coordinator** who will play a key role in supporting our growth from both a Talent Acquisition and HR Operations perspective.
This is a hands\-on position for someone who enjoys recruiting, working closely with hiring managers and candidates, and at the same time being involved in the broader employee lifecycle.
The role offers significant autonomy and the opportunity to actively contribute to the further development of our HR processes rather than simply working within already established structures.

---------
A major focus of the position will be **Talent Acquisition**, particularly for IT, consulting, sales and other specialised profiles.
You will manage recruitment processes end\-to\-end, from understanding the hiring need through to onboarding, while also supporting day\-to\-day HR activities throughout the employee lifecycle.

---------------------
* Manage **full\-cycle recruitment** for technical and non\-technical positions, from job briefing and job posting to sourcing, screening, interviews, offer management and onboarding.
* Conduct candidate interviews independently in **German and English**.
* Develop sourcing strategies and proactively identify suitable candidates, including passive talent.
* Build and maintain talent pipelines for current and future hiring needs.
* Partner closely with hiring managers to understand requirements, challenge profiles where appropriate and advise on recruitment decisions.
* Coordinate external recruitment agencies and other recruiting partners.
* Ensure a positive and professional candidate experience throughout the recruitment process.
* Support employer branding activities and recruitment initiatives.
* Coordinate onboarding and offboarding processes.
* Prepare and manage HR documentation, including contracts, amendments, confirmations and other employee\-related documents.
* Maintain accurate employee data and HR records.
* Support employees and managers with day\-to\-day HR questions.
* Assist with work permits, relocation and other employment\-related administrative processes where required.
* Support payroll preparation and coordination by ensuring that relevant HR data and changes are correctly captured and communicated.
* Contribute to the continuous improvement and further development of HR policies, processes and tools.
* Support additional HR and administrative activities when needed.
* Occasionally travel between Logol’s current and future office locations to support HR activities, onboarding, employee meetings and company initiatives.

-----------------------
* **At least 5 years of relevant experience** in Talent Acquisition, Recruiting and/or HR Coordination.
* Strong hands\-on experience with **end\-to\-end recruitment**, ideally including IT or other specialised professional profiles.
* Proven ability to source candidates proactively and engage passive talent.
* Experience conducting structured candidate interviews and assessing both skills and motivation.
* Strong stakeholder\-management skills and confidence working directly with hiring managers.
* Good understanding of the employee lifecycle, including onboarding, offboarding and HR administration.
* Knowledge of **Swiss HR practices and employment law**; experience with work permits and international employees is an advantage.
* Experience with ATS/HR systems and LinkedIn Recruiter or comparable sourcing tools.
* **Professional German, ideally C1 or equivalent – essential.** You must be comfortable conducting complete recruitment interviews and communicating professionally with candidates and stakeholders in German.
* **Very good English – essential**, as English is our company language.
* Additional languages, particularly Italian or French, are an advantage.
* Swiss HR qualification such as **HR Assistant / HRSE** or comparable further education is an advantage.
* Strong organisational skills, attention to detail and a pragmatic, solution\-oriented approach.
* Willingness to travel occasionally between Logol locations in Switzerland and, where required, other current or future offices.

s.h: The person we are looking for

HR Generalist \& Assistenz Geschäftsleitung (60–80%)
=======================================================
**Du willst HR nicht nur administrieren, sondern wirklich mitgestalten?**
Du arbeitest gerne strukturiert, hältst Fäden zusammen und bist gleichzeitig nahe an Menschen, Führung und Organisation? Dann könnte diese Rolle zu dir passen.
FILADOS ist ein Unternehmen für Wasseraufbereitung mit Sitz in Pratteln. Wir entwickeln und betreiben Lösungen für Gebäudetechnik, Industrie, Gesundheitswesen und weitere anspruchsvolle Anwendungen.
Für unsere zentrale HR\- und Organisationsfunktion suchen wir eine erfahrene Persönlichkeit, die unser Personalwesen operativ verantwortet und gleichzeitig die Geschäftsleitung organisatorisch unterstützt.
Bei uns bist du nicht einfach „HR Administration“. Du bist zentrale Ansprechperson für Mitarbeitende und Führungskräfte, sorgst für professionelle HR\-Prozesse und gestaltest Themen wie Recruiting, Personalentwicklung, interne Kommunikation und Organisation aktiv mit.
**Deine Aufgabe**
Du verantwortest unser operatives HR von A bis Z und arbeitest eng mit dem Vorsitzenden der Geschäftsleitung sowie unseren Führungskräften zusammen.
***HR \& Personalwesen***
* Betreuung der Personaladministration vom Eintritt bis zum Austritt
* Erstellung und Pflege von Arbeitsverträgen, Vertragsänderungen, Bestätigungen und Arbeitszeugnissen
* Pflege von Personalstammdaten und Personaldossiers
* Koordination von Absenzen, Versicherungen, Behörden und weiteren externen Stellen
* Unterstützung von Mitarbeitenden und Führungskräften bei operativen HR\-Fragen
* Überwachung wichtiger Fristen, Pendenzen und personalbezogener Prozesse
***Personalentwicklung \& FILADOS Academy***
* Organisation und Koordination von Weiterbildungen und Schulungen
* Mitarbeit bei Entwicklungs\- und Schulungsplänen
* Organisation und Administration der FILADOS Academy
* Unterstützung beim internen Wissenstransfer
***Assistenz der Geschäftsleitung***
* Vorbereitung und Koordination von Sitzungen, Terminen und Workshops
* Erstellung und Versand von Unterlagen, Protokollen und Pendenzenlisten
* Nachverfolgung von Beschlüssen, Massnahmen, Fristen und Terminen
* Vorbereitung von Übersichten, Auswertungen und Entscheidungsgrundlagen
* Koordination zwischen Geschäftsleitung, Führungskräften und internen Stellen
***Kommunikation \& Organisation***
Je nach Thema wirkst du ausserdem bei der internen und externen Unternehmenskommunikation sowie bei bereichsübergreifenden Projekten mit. Du musst dabei kein Kommunikationsprofi sein. Wichtig ist uns, dass du klar formulierst, Informationen gut strukturierst und gerne dafür sorgst, dass Dinge funktionieren.
**Das bringst du mit**
Wir suchen keine Person, die in jedem HR\-Thema bereits Spezialistin oder Spezialist ist. Wir suchen einen erfahrenen HR\-Generalisten, der Verantwortung übernimmt, strukturiert arbeitet und in einem KMU pragmatisch handeln kann.
* Kaufmännische oder vergleichbare Grundausbildung
* Weiterbildung im Personalwesen, idealerweise HR\-Fachausweis oder vergleichbare Qualifikation
* Mehrere Jahre Erfahrung in einer generalistischen HR\-Funktion
* Solide Kenntnisse des Arbeitsrechts und der Personaladministration
* Erfahrung mit Arbeitsverträgen, Zeugnissen und HR\-Prozessen
* Sehr gute Deutschkenntnisse in Wort und Schrift
* Strukturierte, zuverlässige und selbständige Arbeitsweise
* Hohe Diskretion im Umgang mit Personaldaten und vertraulichen Geschäftsleitungsinformationen
* Freude an der Zusammenarbeit mit Mitarbeitenden und Führungskräften

* Erfahrung in einem KMU
* Recruiting\-Erfahrung
* Erfahrung mit Personalentwicklung oder Weiterbildung
* Erfahrung in der Unterstützung einer Geschäftsleitung
* Interesse an digitalen HR\-Prozessen und modernen Recruiting\-Methoden
**Was dich bei FILADOS erwartet**
***Eine breite Rolle mit sichtbarer Wirkung:*** Du arbeitest nicht in einem engen HR\-Silo, sondern mit Mitarbeitenden, Führungskräften und Geschäftsleitung – und siehst unmittelbar, was deine Arbeit bewirkt.
***Direkter Zugang zur Geschäftsleitung:*** Du arbeitest eng mit dem Vorsitzenden der Geschäftsleitung zusammen und bist organisatorisch nah an den wichtigen Themen des Unternehmens.
***Gestaltungsspielraum:*** Unsere HR\-Prozesse, Personalentwicklung, Academy und Recruiting\-Aktivitäten entwickeln sich weiter. Du kannst diese Entwicklung aktiv mitprägen.
***Selbständigkeit:*** Wir suchen jemanden, der Themen zuverlässig übernimmt, strukturiert und zu Ende bringt.
***Ein KMU mit kurzen Wegen:*** Entscheidungen werden dort getroffen, wo gearbeitet wird. Gute Ideen können umgesetzt werden.
***Ein bewusstes Pensum von 60–80%:*** Die Rolle ist ausdrücklich nicht als klassische 100%\-Corporate\-Funktion angelegt.
Weitere konkrete Rahmenbedingungen und Benefits werden im persönlichen Gespräch erläutert.
**Passt das zu dir?**
Vielleicht arbeitest du heute als HR Generalist, HR Specialist oder HR Manager in einem kleineren Unternehmen und möchtest näher an die Geschäftsleitung und stärker an die Gestaltung. Oder du suchst bewusst eine vielseitige HR\-Rolle mit einem Pensum von 60–80%.
Dann möchten wir dich kennenlernen. Für den ersten Kontakt brauchen wir kein perfektes Motivationsschreiben. Ein Lebenslauf und ein paar Zeilen dazu, warum dich die Rolle interessiert, .

Every 10 minutes, 18 million conversations happen between businesses and consumers around the world.
For decades, the consumer side of those conversations sucked: long queues, robotic menus, repeated explanations, and advice that is often unhelpful. Most people today still cannot simply say what their problem is in natural language when communicating with businesses.
AI changes that. For the first time, companies can have natural conversations with customers at massive scale. Every B2C company - from energy providers to telcos to insurers - will use AI agents to talk to their customers. The number of conversations businesses will handle is going to explode in the coming years.
At telli, we are solving the challenges that come with that shift. Today, leading B2C companies like Sky are already using telli to deploy thousands of voice agents to provide their customers with a new experience.

But building a first voice agent is easy, getting it to drive real outcomes for customers and businesses is the hard part. telli helps companies build, deploy, and improve consumer-facing AI voice agents at scale. This will become one of the most important software categories of the next decade, and we intend to win it.
We are a small, AI-pilled team that likes to solve hard problems. Be it engineering, product, or GTM - we build, experiment, and move fast, while heavily leveraging the capabilities of AI models. All of us like to challenge ourselves and take real ownership over what we do, all while still staying humble and keeping a low-ego culture.
Check out our principles to see how we work.
mission
As the Workplace Operations Intern at telli, you help create the environment our team does its best work in. You support everything around our Berlin office, team events, and workplace experience - and get a front-row seat to how an early-stage AI company operates day to day. Perfect if you want to learn how a fast-moving startup works from the inside.

keep our Berlin office running smoothly - supplies, equipment, and making the space a place people want to be
support planning and running team events: offsites, onsite interviews, team dinners, and community events
help new joiners have a great first day - desk setup, hardware, and access
coordinate with vendors and service providers for everything office-related
learn to build small automations around workplace ops (ordering, inventory, requests) with AI and no-code tools
jump in on ad-hoc tasks and support the team wherever help is needed

s.h: what makes you a great fit
s.t:
you are hands-on and not afraid of doing unglamorous work
you're organized, reliable, and notice details others miss
you're curious about tools and automation and pick up new things fast
you take initiative and don't wait for detailed instructions
you're a strong communicator in both English and German
you're a host at heart - you enjoy creating great experiences for others

s.h: you may not make a good fit if

you aren't comfortable juggling multiple tasks at once
you prefer working fully remote - this role lives in the office
you'd rather observe than roll up your sleeves

About 9fin
9fin is the AI platform powering global debt markets — the world’s largest asset class at over $145 trillion.
Debt markets are vast, global, and mission-critical, yet still run on fragmented data, PDFs, and manual workflows. 9fin replaces this broken infrastructure with a single platform that centralises proprietary credit data, deep analysis, and high-value workflows across global markets.
Today, 9fin powers teams at 300+ blue-chip institutions worldwide, including global banks, asset managers, private equity firms, law firms, and advisors. The business is scaling at exceptional speed, with rapid expansion in the US and best-in-class retention driven by deep workflow adoption.
We’re at a defining inflection point. With proven product-market fit and strong, global market pull, 9fin is accelerating toward becoming the category-defining platform for debt markets worldwide.
The opportunity
Our People Partners are the eyes and ears of the organisation, embedded within their functional areas to be a sounding board for leaders, support managers and enable teams to thrive.

The People Partnering team operate on a strategic and tactical level, ensuring the people elements are in place for teams to effectively deliver their strategic objectives (think org design, upskilling, succession planning) whilst also offering one on one support, both structured and ad hoc, to those who need it most.
We're hiring an experienced, driven Senior People Partner to partner with our Chief Content Officer and the Content (Editorial, Legals, Credit, Distressed) team. Content is scaling fast across the UK and US, and we need a Senior People Partner who can move at pace, get to grips with what the team actually does, and hold their own with senior editorial and analytical leaders.
You'll be fully embedded in the Content team, with a real voice in leadership meetings, editorial rituals and off-sites. You'll know the leads, managers and rising talent well enough to catch the people issues long before they show up in engagement scores or exit interviews.
Every day is different, but here's an example of the kind of things you'll work on:
Strategic
Trusted advisor to your leaders : You'll be the first person Content leadership calls on anything people-related: the confidant, sounding board and thought partner they think alongside, not the person they update after the fact. That kind of trust is earned over time, through showing up and being willing to have the harder conversation when it matters.
Right hand person to the CCO: You know how he thinks about content and his organisation, and are confident acting as his proxy with his leaders to get them to where they need to be.
Locked in on what the team is trying to achieve : You know Content's goals, what its leaders and teams do. You bring solutions, not just observations, and follow them through to completion.
Fully embedded in your team : You're in the rituals, Slack channels and meetings that matter, so you've got a real read on how the team actually works. You cut through the noise to name the actual issue and get it resolved quickly and respectfully.
Catching things early : You join the dots across 1:1s, skips, engagement data and your own observations to surface people risks while they're still small and easy to fix. You coach leaders and managers to build the same instinct.
Org design : You advise on org shape, spot gaps and flag future risk areas. You make sure the right people are doing the right jobs at the right level as Content scales across regions and coverage.
Talent management : You know who the key talent is and you work with leaders to develop, stretch and reward them. You support leaders to identify their successors and build the development plans that get them ready. You work proactively with the Talent team on the pipelines for roles you can already see coming.
Learning & development : You spot where Content teams need to grow — editorial craft, analytical rigour, management skill, leadership development — and you lead the training that plugs the gap. A big part of that is upskilling managers to handle people issues themselves, early and well, rather than escalating them to the CCO. You diagnose early, source or build the right thing, and hold a bar for what impact should look like once it's landed.
Reward : You use solid data to inform our salary bands and keep compensation fair across the team, with D&I front of mind. You coach leaders and managers through promotion and salary reviews so decisions are thoughtful, equitable and defensible.
Performance : You help leaders and managers get the best out of their teams, surfacing blockers, coaching through them, and making sure feedback and training actually land. You hold a high bar yourself and help leaders hold one too.
Hands up for the bigger stuff : You take on projects that improve the People function as a whole, not just your patch. You scope them properly, influence stakeholders, manage the risks and dependencies, and ship on time.
Tactical
Employee Relations (ER) : Following UK employment law, navigating all employee relations within your business area, including but not limited to: managing Performance Improvement Plans (PIPs), resolving claims and grievances in line with policy, probation management, maternity and paternity cases, flexible working requests, conflict management and mediation, and any other employee-to-employee issue that comes up, both formally and informally.
Embedding people products : Working with the wider Partnering team to embed our people products and systems, delivering training, championing adoption and being the go-to person for questions. Delivering product feedback to the wider team on a regular basis.
Data : Pulling and analysing the right data to help managers and leaders make good calls and adding the context that turns numbers into something your leaders can actually use.
Wellbeing support : 1:1 support to employees when they need it, and making sure they know what mental and physical health support is on offer. Supporting managers through those conversations too.
Cultural ambassador : Working with leaders and managers to reinforce the right behaviours in teams. Being a role model yourself for our values and ways of working, especially as the London office grows.

s.h: This role will be a great fit if you
s.t:
Take real accountability for pushing back on leaders — not just flagging a concern and moving on, but staying with it until the right decision gets made.
Can confidently challenge executives and their most senior leaders when it matters, as a true partner rather than a service function.
Are properly curious about the business you support. You'll want to understand how Content produces its analysis, what makes a great desk, and what separates a good journalist from a world class one. You ask questions until you get to the real answer.
Are a strong influencer, able to help others look at things from different perspectives and understand the 'why' behind decisions. Comfortable pushing back on leaders and managers when needed, and know when to step back and let them make their own call.

Pennylane vous offre l'opportunité de grandir au sein d'une entreprise en pleine croissance.
Ici, votre expertise contribuera directement à aider les entrepreneurs à reprendre le contrôle de leurs finances. Découvrez un lieu où vos compétences seront valorisées et où vous pourrez façonner l'avenir de la gestion financière.
Notre vision
Notre ambition est de devenir le logiciel de pilotage financier préféré des PMEs européennes.
Nous aidons les entrepreneurs à se débarrasser des tâches chronophages liées à la comptabilité et à la finance, tout en leur donnant accès à des informations financières clés pour les aider à prendre les meilleures décisions pour leur entreprise.
Parallèlement, nous aidons les cabinets d'expertise-comptable, en leur permettant de passer moins de temps sur des tâches redondantes et répétitives, et plus de temps sur la partie conseil et accompagnement de leurs clients.
À propos de Pennylane
Pennylane est une des FinTech à la plus forte croissance en France, et souhaite bientôt adresser le marché européen.

s.h: En 5 ans d'existence, nous sommes parvenus à
s.t:
💻 Nous positionner sur le marché comme un éditeur de solution de comptabilité et de gestion financière innovant
💰 Lever un total de 400 millions d'euros, auprès d'investisseurs de renom, dont Sequoïa, le fonds phare de la Silicon Valley, connu pour avoir soutenu Google, Facebook, Airbnb, Stripe, Paypal et bien d'autres à leur début
👨‍👩‍👧‍👦 Passer de 7 cofondateurs à une équipe de 1300 collaborateurs, avec une note moyenne de 4,9/5 sur Glassdoor et 94% des évaluateurs Glassdoor qui recommanderaient PL à leurs proches!
🌍 Construire une équipe internationale composée de collaborateurs issus de 25 pays différents, avec une culture du télétravail très flexible
🤝 Gagner la confiance de milliers d'utilisateurs et obtenir d'excellents retours
🚀 Déjà plus de 1 300,000 TPE/PME et plus de 7000 cabinets d’expertise-comptable utilisent Pennylane en France !
Contexte du rôle
Pennylane accélère son expansion européenne (France, Allemagne, Espagne) dans un contexte de scale rapide, où la structuration des organisations et la cohérence managériale multi-pays deviennent critiques.
En tant que Head of HRBP (N-1 COMEX) , tu construis une fonction HRBP qui est un veritable levier de support à la performance du business : tu influences les décisions d’organisation, sécurises la montée en maturité managériale et aides l’entreprise à passer des caps de transformation.
L’ IA est un pilier du rôle : tu anticipes son impact sur les métiers, accompagnes l’adoption et outilles la fonction People pour gagner en efficacité et en prédictibilité.
Missions principales
Ce rôle nécessite des allers-retours fréquents au HQ de Pennylane situé à Paris, chaque semaine, parfois sans nuitée.
Ce rôle nécessite de parler anglais quotidiennement.
Définir et piloter la stratégie HRBP alignée sur les priorités business, les enjeux de scale et l’expansion internationale.
Être le/la partenaire stratégique du COMEX : challenger les orientations d’organisation, éclairer les arbitrages et sécuriser l’exécution.
Anticiper et conduire les transformations organisationnelles (design d’organisation, évolutions de périmètres, montée en compétences managériales).
Construire une approche data-driven et prédictive : KPIs, modèles d’alerte (attrition, engagement, performance, capacité), plans d’action.
Piloter la cohérence People multi-pays : harmoniser là où ça crée de la valeur, tout en respectant les contraintes locales (cadres légaux, culture, pratiques).
Manager, développer et faire évoluer une équipe de 8 HRBPs , en renforçant posture d’influence, priorisation et qualité de delivery.
Structurer la gouvernance HRBP (rituels, operating model, répartition run/projets) et accélérer l’excellence opérationnelle via outils modernes (Workday, agents internes).
Profil recherché
8–12 ans d’expérience RH, avec une expérience d’au moins 3 ans en tant que Head of HRBP / Head of People / DRH dans un environnement déjà très mature ou en forte croissance.
Expérience tangible de construction/structuration d’une fonction HR/HRBP (process, outils, gouvernance, recrutement d’équipe).

Summary: The primary purpose of this position is: To serve as administrator and technical expert for the Military Personnel Flight's (MPF) Military Personnel Data Systems (MILPDS) and Air Force Integrated Pay and Personnel System (AFIPPS) once implemented.

Position administers internet-based, Oracle-based applications and provides technical systems support to users in the MPF and installation wide. Position also manages or coordinates technical support for the MPF required for communication and on and off-base. Strong Military Human Resource (HR) experience supporting information technology is a must.

Duties: Administers Military Personnel Data Systems.

Administers internet-based, Oracle-based Military Personnel Data System (MilPDS) applications and provides technical support and advisory services to include system security, user account management, printer and peripheral management, user access and connectivity, and monitoring application software changes or releases.

Accomplish MPF automation planning, coordination, and implementation. Plans and provides customer assistance/training. Provides personnel systems management advisory services. Participates in special projects and initiatives and performs special assignments.

SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE: Applicants must have at least one (1) year of specialized experience at the next lower grade GS-09, or equivalent in other pay systems.

Examples of specialized experience includes utilizing established techniques and requirements for data processing, documentation procedures, standard data elements and codes; availability of utility routines; customary fact-finding approaches; and decision logic tables in order to monitor subject-matter personnel computer systems; evaluate brands of computer equipment; facilitate user interface and access to computer systems; reviewing software available from vendors; use an established database and output requirements; provide user training; and perform standardized disc recovery operations.

Utilizing work processes, data models, work rules, file/database design/structure and content, equipment, internal computer process, applications, and utility programs, to advise on alternative approaches, to identify problems and plan and implement solutions, and to collaborate with design center personnel in effecting needing changes.

OR EDUCATION: Successfully completed a Ph.D. or equivalent doctoral degree or 3 full years of progressively higher-level graduate education leading to such a degree or LL.M. in a field which demonstrates the knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to perform the work of the position.

NOTE: You must submit a copy of your transcripts with your application. OR COMBINATION OF EXPERIENCE AND EDUCATION: A combination of specialized experience and education as described above.

Having less than the full amount of specialized experience required but more than 2 years of graduate level education with a major or subject area related to the position to be filled. NOTE: You must submit a copy of your transcripts with your application.

FEDERAL TIME-IN-GRADE (TIG) REQUIREMENT FOR GENERAL SCHEDULE (GS) POSITIONS: Merit promotion applicants must meet applicable time-in-grade requirements to be considered eligible. One year at the GS-09 level is required to meet the time-in-grade requirements for the GS-11 level.

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES (KSAs): Your qualifications will be evaluated on the basis of your level of knowledge, skills, abilities and/or competencies in the following areas: Knowledge of automated data processing functions, techniques, and capabilities including relational database principles; Structured Query Language (SQL), microcomputer operation, the network operating system, and MilPDS.

Ability to gather facts and use effective analytical and evaluative methods to accurately assess information and make sound decisions. Ability to develop improvements and design new personnel work methods and procedures using automated systems. PART-TIME OR UNPAID EXPERIENCE: Credit will be given for appropriate unpaid and or part-time work.

You must clearly identify the duties and responsibilities in each position held and the total number of hours per week.

VOLUNTEER WORK EXPERIENCE: Refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service Programs (i.e., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student and social).

Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge and skills that can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

We’re looking for an HR Administrator to be our regional presence in Germany, someone who takes genuine pride in getting the details right and who enjoys being the trusted, go-to person for People and HR matters.
This is a hands-on, varied role covering two connected halves: On the People side, you’ll support the full employee lifecycle for our EU-based population, working closely with, and reporting into, the HR Manager (UK/EU); from onboarding and contracts through to day-to-day queries, payroll inputs, and offboarding.

On the office side, you’ll take ownership of day-to-day administration for our Germany offices, keeping things running smoothly for the team based there.

You’ll be the face of People and HR ATG in Germany: a proactive, organised self-starter who is comfortable working independently, escalating the right things to the HR Manager, and building trusted relationships with employees at every level.
Tasks

· HR Administration & Employee Lifecycle (Germany)

· Act as the first point of contact for Germany-based employees on day-to-day HR queries, policies and procedures, escalating and supporting complex matters with the HR Manager (UK/EU)

· Support the end-to-end employee lifecycle for Germany and EU employees, including onboarding, contract changes, promotions, transfers and offboarding

· Prepare and issue employment contracts, contract amendments and other employment documentation in line with local legal requirements

· Maintain accurate, up-to-date employee records and personnel files for the Germany population, ensuring GDPR compliance

· Coordinate onboarding and induction for new starters in Germany and EU, including right-to-work checks, equipment set up, and welcome activities

· Support recruitment activity for Germany-based roles, including scheduling interviews, liaising with candidates and hiring managers, and maintaining the applicant tracking system

· Prepare and submit monthly Germany payroll inputs (e.g. new starters, leavers, changes), working closely with the HR Manager and the Mexico Service Centre

· Support benefits administration for German employees, including pension, health insurance and other statutory benefits

· Help ensure compliance with German and EU labour law and statutory requirements, flagging risks or changes to the HR Manager (UK/EU)

· Support the administration of performance review cycles and any local training or development activity

· Provide administrative support to the HR Manager on EU and Germany-related HR projects, audits and reporting
Office Administration (Germany)

· Act as the main point of contact for day-to-day office administration in the German offices

· Manage office supplies, equipment and vendor relationships

· Support health & safety compliance for the Berlin office, including risk assessments and fire safety procedures

· Organise office events, socials and wellbeing initiatives for the Berlin team, in partnership with the HR Manager and the wider Employee Experience calendar

· Manage incoming and outgoing post, deliveries, and visitor arrangements for the Berlin office

· Support new starters with desk set up, access passes/keys, and induction to the office

· Liaise with building management/landlord on facilities issues

· Support ad hoc administrative and office management tasks as required

· Some experience in an HR administration, HR coordinator, or office administration role (internships and placements considered)

· Working knowledge of German employment law and HR practices

· Fluent in German and English, both written and spoken

· Strong organisational skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities and competing deadlines

· Excellent attention to detail and accuracy, particularly with employee data and documentation

· A proactive, can-do attitude, comfortable working independently as the HR and office presence on the ground in Germany

· Strong interpersonal and communication skills, with the ability to build trust with employees at all levels

· Ability to manage confidential information with discretion

· Comfortable using HRIS, payroll or office management systems (training provided)

· Studying towards or holding a relevant HR qualification (e.g. IHK Personalfachkaufmann/-frau or equivalent)

· Experience supporting an international or matrixed organisation

· Experience with office management or facilities coordination

Founded by leading automotive manufacturers, we operate Europe’s largest high-power charging network across 24 countries, enabling seamless long-distance travel for EV drivers. With thousands of charging points already in operation and significant expansion ahead, IONITY is evolving beyond charging infrastructure into a broader mobility, energy and digital platform.
As Senior People Ops & Payroll Manager , you'll ensure IONITY's People Operations and payroll run accurately, on time and with care across our multi-country European setup. This is a hands-on role for someone who knows payroll inside out, enjoys making processes cleaner and more scalable, and wants the admin side of work to feel effortless for employees.
You'll own the payroll cycle end to end, keep our employee data and lifecycle processes in great shape, and be the go-to partner for our external payroll providers, People Partners and employees.

About Blackthorn
Blackthorn turns any organization's Salesforce® CRM into event planning software powered by their connected data. We're a growing, distributed team with teammates across the globe, and we build Salesforce-native tools that help teams create events, engage attendees, process payments, and measure success — all without leaving their CRM.

Our customers range from tiny nonprofits to global corporations, and our products are known for going live in hours, not weeks. We believe the best enterprise software should feel as intuitive as the apps you use every day.
Why our work matters
Most event management tools force teams to juggle disconnected systems, wrestle with flimsy integrations, and spend more time syncing data than planning events.

We're building the alternative: a connected platform inside Salesforce that gives organizations richer analytics to prove event ROI, better attendee experiences through personalization and automation, and the flexibility to fit any workflow.

Every feature we ship helps our customers spend less time on logistics and more time on the events themselves.
What the job will bring you
A deep level of satisfaction through ownership of your role. You'll get more autonomy than at other companies (our team has told us). Connection. Our team is tightly knit, assisted through occasional team meetups (as we're remote). Challenge. We're trying to move as quickly as possible. This is not for you if you want to sit back and chill. As Ray Dalio says about life, "Meaningful work and meaningful relationships" provide meaning to life. We aim to bring this.
